comment: At 1280 by 800 and at scale 2 the default layout leaves room to paint. The shipped default with five layers, on a 1280 by 800 panel at scale 1, at scale 2 and back, the Window menu at scale 2, then a 1280 by 1024 panel at both scales, the 4K panel and a 1920 by 1080 one at scale 2, Tab, scale 2 and Tab again, and last the Workspace page's scale row held at 200 per cent on the 1280 by 800 panel. The windows array of each state says which dockers are open and where, and docker_layout says default at every step.
01, 1280 by 800 at scale 1: the left column's floors are 5 more than its height, so Reference closes and nothing overlaps. The columns stand on 680 and the painting keeps 600 of 1280.

02, 1280 by 800 at scale 2, a host of 640 by 400: Layers closes for height and Tool Options for width, the Brush Presets closed, the toolbox and the Colour Picker stay open, and the painting keeps 270 of 640 between them.
03, the Window menu at scale 2 still lists the four dockers the fit closed, unticked, where the shipped order has them.
04, back at scale 1 the three the width and height had closed are open again where 01 had them, and the layout is still default.
05, 1280 by 1024 at scale 1: all six open, as a suite of its own holds.
06, 1280 by 1024 at scale 2, a host of 640 by 512: the same two dockers as 02.
07, the 4K panel at scale 2, a host of 1920 by 1080: the file as written, all six open.

08, 1920 by 1080 at scale 2, a host of 960 by 540: Layers closes for height, the Reference and the Brush Presets stay closed as shipped, and Tool Options and the Colour Picker give up width to their floors rather than one of them closing.
09, Tab, scale 2 and Tab again: the way back shows what Tab hid and the reflow after it closes the same four as 02, which stood where scale 1 had them.
10, the scale row held at 200 per cent on the 1280 by 800 panel: its hint says the dockers open now would leave less than 40 per cent of the window to paint in.
11, the same row moved back to 100 per cent says nothing of the kind.
